notes.C2: The empty red-bordered yellow circle forbids vehicle traffic, distinct from C1's one-direction entry ban and the narrower vehicle classes.
notes.C3: Car and motorcycle with diagonal bar match the motor-vehicle ban; the class-II moped exclusion and supplementary-panel extension are preserved.
notes.C4: The front-view car symbol legally covers motor vehicles with more than two wheels, not passenger cars alone.
notes.C5: The motorcycle/rider restriction includes class-I mopeds; class-II mopeds are not silently added to this sign.
notes.C6: The trailer symbol is not a blanket ban on every trailer; the semi-trailer/slapkarra exclusions and panel extensions match the source.
notes.C7: The lorry access prohibition applies to heavy-lorry class, not all goods vehicles and not merely overtaking.
notes.C8: The tractor picture does not replace the legal class boundary; tractor-b/class-I equipment extensions require a panel as the dated source states.
notes.C9: The orange-centred goods symbol concerns orange-plate-regulated dangerous loads; T23 tunnel-category scope is retained, unlike a ban on any hazardous item.
notes.C10: The bicycle symbol covers bicycles/class-II mopeds, with class-I extension requiring a panel; it is distinct from C11's moped-only scope.
notes.C11: The visible moped is correctly distinguished from a bicycle; the sign's class-II/class-I panel boundary is not broadened.
notes.C12: Horse and cart indicates animal-drawn vehicles; it does not merely prohibit riding, unlike C14.
notes.C13: The tracked vehicle pictogram represents off-road motor vehicles/trailers, and the off-road-wagon exception needs a panel.
notes.C14: The mounted horse prohibits riding; leading a riding animal needs a separate panel extension.
notes.C15: The walking figure is pedestrian access prohibition; no general all-traffic prohibition is invented.
notes.C16: Side arrows and 2.2 m identify width, including the load, distinct from the displayed height/length signs.
notes.C17: Top/bottom arrows and 3.5 m identify height; the source's below-4.5-m restricted-clearance scope is retained.
notes.C18: The 20 m/double arrow correctly identifies maximum vehicle-or-combination length and the neutral description correctly says lorry. Full-size inspection shows a single lorry, contradicting the shared vehicle-and-trailer variant/study caption (DEF-10E-001).
notes.C19: Two cars and 50 m specify minimum gap to a motor vehicle ahead in the same direction, not a route length or maximum gap.
notes.C20: The 12 t sign limits actual gross weight of a vehicle, not registered totalvikt or axle load.
notes.C21: The lorry/trailer over 30 t depicts a vehicle/combination gross-weight limit; it is distinct from the single-vehicle C20 depiction.
notes.C22: BK3 is a bearing-capacity regime, not a direct 3-tonne limit; axle/weight details must be checked separately.
notes.C23: One axle under 6 t identifies axle load, unlike total gross weight or a two-axle bogie limit.
notes.C24: Two axle symbols under 10 t identify bogie load rather than the whole vehicle's weight.
notes.C25: The left-bending arrow matches the no-left-turn variant; the source limits the relevant junction or explicitly panel-extended stretch.
notes.C26: The inverted-U arrow is specifically a U-turn ban; a panel can extend it across more than one junction.
